Python.description: Python is a versatile programming language widely used in backend development, automation, data science and AI.
Python.importance: Python is a core skill for backend developers and is commonly used to build APIs and scalable applications.
practice: Build a command-line expense tracker.
Create a Python application that reads and processes CSV files.
Build a small project using OOP and exception handling.

SQL.description: SQL is a language used to store, retrieve and manipulate data in relational databases.
SQL.importance: Backend applications use SQL to manage user accounts, application data and database operations.
topics: WHERE, ORDER BY and GROUP BY
practice: Write queries to retrieve and filter student records.
Create a database for an online bookstore.
Solve SQL exercises involving joins and subqueries.

Flask.description: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework used to build web applications and APIs.
Flask.importance: Helps Python developers create backend services and REST APIs.
practice: Build a basic Flask application.
Create a REST API with multiple endpoints.
Build a CRUD application connected to a database.

Django.description: Django is a high-level Python web framework designed for building secure and maintainable web applications.
Django.importance: Provides built-in tools for authentication, database operations and application development.
practice: Build a student management application.
Create user registration and login functionality.
Build a CRUD application using Django ORM.

FastAPI.description: FastAPI is a modern Python framework for building high-performance APIs with automatic documentation.
FastAPI.importance: Useful for developing modern backend services and integrating Python applications with frontend systems.
practice: Build a basic FastAPI application.
Create CRUD endpoints for a task manager.
Connect an API to a relational database.

REST API.description: REST APIs allow different software applications to communicate through standardized HTTP requests and responses.
REST API.importance: Backend developers use REST APIs to connect frontend applications, databases and external services.
practice: Design REST endpoints for a library application.
Test API requests using an API testing tool.
Build a CRUD REST API using Flask or FastAPI.

Git.description: Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in source code.
Git.importance: Helps developers maintain code history, work with branches and collaborate on software projects.
practice: Create a local Git repository.
Practice branching and merging.
Create and resolve a merge conflict.

GitHub.description: GitHub is a platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on software development.
GitHub.importance: Helps developers showcase projects, collaborate with teams and maintain professional code repositories.
practice: Publish a Python project on GitHub.
Write a professional project README.
Practice creating branches and pull requests.

Linux.description: Linux is an open-source operating system widely used for servers and software development environments.
Linux.importance: Backend developers frequently use Linux environments for application deployment, server management and automation.
practice: Practice navigating directories using terminal commands.
Create and manage files using shell commands.
Write a basic shell script to automate a repetitive task.

Docker.description: Docker is a platform used to package applications and their dependencies into containers.
Docker.importance: Helps developers build, deploy and run applications consistently across different environments.
practice: Understand the difference between images and containers.
Containerize a simple Python application.
Run a multi-container application using Docker Compose.

AWS.description: AWS is a cloud computing platform offering services for hosting, storage, databases and application deployment.
AWS.importance: Helps developers deploy and manage scalable applications using cloud infrastructure.
practice: Learn the purpose of EC2 and S3.
Explore basic cloud architecture concepts.
Study how a web application can be deployed on AWS.
